Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Vegas 2 was one of the games I played most on the playstation 3 console, but sadly when I went to the Playstation 4 I could no longer play Vegas 2 as the console did not support the game :( but after a while I came to pc and I saw the game on sale and after buying it I can say it definetly gave me good memories of the good old days on the playstation 3.
Now I know your probaly thinking Where's the review!? but don't worry this is where this story takes me, When i first played it on the ps3 it blew my mind and I was blown away at how much there was to unlock and also how many acheivements there was to get!
Now on the pc version of the game it looked even more beautiful than it did on the console version, The pc version has much more brighter shades of colours and lighting effects, it has more features due to mods which the console does not support so your getting alot more with what you buy!
Multiplayer is okay on the game but not the best I would say just stick to the Main story line and also the terroist hunt missions. You want to level up as much as you can in the game to unlock everything in the game but like everything that takes time, so the more you play the more you unlock :)
Overall: I would give this game a full 10/10 ! Everything about this game is great and just beautiful, full of tactics to use and loads of equipment to use! The only downfall is the vs multiplayer but apart from that it is great!

Creature Clicker is a very unremarkable clicking game that has a really bad interface.
To start, this game is almost an exact copy of other clicker games. There really is nothing remarkable about this compared to other games. The idea of tryign to integrate "pokemon" like creatures to collect and level up is really nothign special or impotant as well.
Additionally, the interface is terrible. There is no streamlined place to buy stuff, view things, and a lot of the menu things you ahve to guess and check to see what they do and what they are.
The only benifit of this game is that there are a ton of really easy achievements. When I mean a ton, I mean a ton. IN the first 10 minutes of playing this, I had so many acheivements that my screen was filled. If you want to increase your achievement count, this is a great game to do that.
Overall, not really a special game that is definitly lacking purpose. Before this game gets fleshed out a bit more and improved upon, there is no reason to actually get this game.
Rating: 3.9/10
Recommend Price: $0.09 or below

Well...here we have another clicker game, but as it stands, its one of the more decent ones.  However, you need to keep it open to gain anything. (There are currently no offline rewards)

For what it's worth, it's nice to know that

You may end up leaving the game open for several hours hoping for a proper chest drop to give you the item drops you want.  As you idle for long enough (over 200 hours from my perspective).
So...to recap (and because it's been requested...:
PROS:
+  A clicker game that quickly grows casual.
+  Not a lot of clicking involved.
+  Graphics are decent and are well-animated.
+  Tons of easy achievements.
CONS:
-  If you're addicted to clicking, then this game may disappoint.
-  No offline benefits.
-  An improvement is needed in order to increase epic item drops.
Now for the important question.  "Is it worth buying"?  It's currently priced at $2, which seems to be a bit much.  However, if priced at $1, I'd say it's fairly priced.

Onto the actual content.

Bernard is kind of a ridiculously hard fight that I've been struggling with, but it's incredibly fun. All in all, this was *very* worth it for me.

Furi mode will most likely be pretty easy as he does nothing really crazy, with his final phase being fairly intense as most, save for the first two bosses of the game, are.
It's also nice to see a lot of flare put into the phase transition animations and the clashes.  It's not just a knock down and stand up for the next phase.  Pretty entertaining.
Furier is very fun and a good challenge, it makes you focus on your spacing, counters, dash distance, and everything. It's enjoyable and well done.

The hiden overtuned crazy mode optional boss of this game.  He will mimic all of the other bosses of the game to an extreme degree.  That being said. the fight still does feel very new dispite basically taking crazy mode version of previous bosses.
Two negative points about this boss is the song for him is just a remix of the first and last bosses (although very good songs/remixes, still not a new song) and Bernard himself has no talking/voice. Just the grunting sounds of the Chain.
Overall if you liked Furi this game is worth it. At $2 a boss this dlc is more or less the same deal as the main game if you buy it during a $10-$15 sale so have at it.

Beginning with a pointedly vague premise of your being some kind of detective on the trail of the titular missing child, the game barely holds your hand as you discover your paranormal investigative abilities and begin to piece together a series of strange events in a remote countryside. That lack of hand holding is more a part of the gameplay than one might initially realize as it ultimately provokes a sort of trial and error process that is in itself an investigation. Despite a few fairly simple puzzles, the game is mostly about discovery. While primarily linear, there are various clues and revelations lying just off the beaten path, many of which ultimately need to be discovered to complete the game, but that (whether found later or during the course of your primary investigation) don’t stymie the pace of the game.
The game’s visuals are excellent, featuring not only the river valley vistas seen in the early part of the game, but beautifully dilapidated interiors and dank caves as well. The audio as well is great, with a near perfect score, quality voice acting, and immersive environmental sound. The GUI overlays are brilliant and are realized in such a manner as not feel like an interface, but instead like an extension of the protagonist’s investigative abilities. The ultimate result is a greater sense of immersion and that is a large part of Ethan Carter’s triumph.
Throughout the nearly four hours I spent with The Vanishing of Ethan Carter I was almost completely enraptured by it, spurred on both by a sense of wonderment at the world before my eyes and also by a drive to discover the truth of the mystery at hand. It’s difficult to talk about the story at all without spoiling anything except to say that even when predictable, Ethan Carter delivers with a compelling emotional gravitas. I honestly can’t recommend this game enough to fans of first person adventure games, especially Amenisia, Gone Home, or Dear Esther. The Vanishing of Ethan Carter is worth picking up at any price.

HellDivers is a Hardcore, 4-player co-op, top-down shooter that seems to be a hybrid of Alien Swarm, Magicka, and Diablo. Thematically, you'll be reminded of every Sci-Fi trope that you can imagine as you travel around the galaxy, meet new and interesting species, and act as an ambassador of Democracy. Think.... Starship troopers.
Positives:
+The action and gameplay of shooting up aliens as a spaceman is very well done.
+The progression system system is very well-done. Leveling is as you'd expect- get levels, unlock skins and weapons. Players can also unlock new strategems (powers) by playing through a series of missions successfully. Lastly, players must accrue research points (through leveling and collecting samples on maps) to upgrade their gear. This is a sort of talent tree for your character.
+Equipping your character individually, as well as a team, presents a lot of interesting and meaningful choices. You only have 4 strategem (power) slots, a weapon, and perk (big power) that you can equip. Much of the fun is the trial and error of different loadouts for you and for your team.
+There is a huge variety of weaponry. Most of the weapons are different enough that there's not really a 'super weapon' but rather weapons that fit a specific roll or style.
+There is a massive variety of powers that you can unlock. Think of Guild Wars/Guild Wars 2 - the possibilities are immense.
+The combined arms aspect of the game is well-done.
+BIG ROBOTS that you can use to spread Democracy.
Negatives:
-There are occasionally steam network/game connectivity issues. If you disconnect from a mission,  you lose your progress in collecting science samples (which are really important.)
-You absolutely must stay on the same screen as your teammates. This can get a little hectic/difficult if your cursors are scattered all over the place, constraining your ability to see what's going on around you.
-The controls can be a little hard to master. Your mouse cursor will move faster than your characters/turrets can turn. Ultimately, there's some balance to this... but many PC players will find this to be a bit sluggish.
-When playing with randoms, there is a (small) potential that you will encounter a hacker; reportedly, a hacker can increase your XP/science points to max, somewhat thwarting your progression.
Overall, this is a great game to play with your buddies looking for a Coop game, or with random folks and pubbies. The action is good, and there is a lot of value in the hilarious wipes that you'll surely incur.

A prequel to the long-running Ys series, Ys Origins tells the story of Darm Tower before the events of Ys I & II. Unlike most Ys games, you don't play as familiar, red-haired protagonist Adol Christin, but rather one of two characters (there is also a 'secret' third character), the axe-wielding Yunica and the mage Hugo. This is a different take on the series than most entries, and is a welcome change as there is a lot of variety with the playstyles of each character, and this also adds to the replay value as you can play through the game multiple times with different characters, the story being slightly different for each as well.
The story is rather bare-bones, but mildly interesting, particularly if you are an Ys fan or a fan of traditional fantasy storylines. Nothing to set the world on fire, but the main characters are likable (particularly Yunica) and the story does not get in the way of the game's main strength: the fast-paced, action-RPG combat. If you've never played an Ys game, particularly the older titles, the game plays as a mix of a top-down hack n' slash and a 2.5 platformer. Many of the skills you gain have dual uses for both platforming and combat, and there is a decent variety of abilities. That being said, there is much more combat than platforming in the game, and while the platforming can be occasionally frustrating, the combat is where the series, and this game in particular, truly shines. Combat requires you to quickly chain together attacks, make smart use of your skills, and avoid enemy attacks by dodging and jumping. Basic enemies are not too difficult, though there is a wide variety of enemy types to fight, all with their different skillsets and strategies. The bosses are the main attraction, being both difficult and surprisingly epic for a game without state-of-the-art graphics.
One more thing about this game, and the Ys series as a whole: the music is FANTASTIC! Some of the best videogame music I have ever heard is from this series, and this entry keeps the bar set high. There are quite a few stellar tracks, many of which are boss themes. Overall, I would reccomend this game to any fan of the series, any fan of action RPG's, and any fan of Japanese games. If none of these categories apply to you, then pick this gem up on sale. Trust me, you will not be dissapointed, and maybe you'll become another fan of this underappreciated (but spectacular) series.

Rainbow Six Vegas 2 is a direct sequel to the R6: Vegas. Kinda funny at that, as main hero is different but you control same squad. Still a tactical FPS, still without planning stage that older games had. It was released in 2008 and made by Ubisoft Montreal.
It was also released for Xbox 360 and PS3. I heard that the only difference is that ability to put your face over your avatar with facecam is much improved in PC version. Oh, yes, and consoles also supported split-screen mode. No such thing on PC here.
Technically, I encountered very few problem. First, quitting from gameplay into main menu would give me black screen. It was easy to fix just by alt-tabbing though. And second, I am still confused why bombs keep loudly tick even after your teammate disarms them. It's either very strange design or a bug too. It sure made some scenes quite awkward.
It also has in-game achievements, but not linked to Steam. Hey, Steam overlay works now at least.
As for multiplayer, it's alive. Ubisoft said something about not providing servers anymore long time ago, but the only thing it means is that you can't register new account in this game. BUT you can use your UPlay account instead, putting your email as login. And password as password.
People mostly play Terrorist Hunt mode, which is incredibly fun. I also seen coop servers around, but this game was on sale not long time ago so no promises that they will stay. It supports coop only for 2 players after all, so usually people just invite their friend. There also were few versus servers, but people only play Deathmatch and Team Deathmatch now. Not every server was password protected here, good thing.
And well, what can I say, it's a direct sequel and a much better PC port as well. Though this time it has global leveling system, so you aren't likely to use shield on your first playthrough. Which I am not sure that I approve. Talking of it, there is also character customization that also applies to single-player and coop, as you play as custom account called Bishop instead of Logan. And you can slap your face over the character head too. Most of the times it's going to apply eyes to forehead. Or you can apply drawing, if you are creative enough and willing to.
And hey, at least this time around the game actually looks good. Much better than Vegas 1. Well, one of the reasons for that is because PC port was made with widesceen in mind this time around, supporting all the resolution. But most importantly, Ubisoft finally realized that applying brown filter doesn't make it next gen. What you mean that X360 isn't next gen anymore?
Music and setting are much more varied around as well, it's not just Vegas now. Sadly, I noticed that sound seems to not always be mixed good. At least I had trouble hearing everything I am being told.
Oh, and plot sucks. Alright, it's fine, but nothing amazing.
There are very little new gameplay mechanic. I was dissapointed there, I surely would have loved it if they let you command two squads at same time. But nope, just one squad with same two rainbow bros. Oh well. I can easily list new features. First, you can sprint, with very limited stamina, always forgot that it exists. And more importantly, you can finally order AI teammates to throw grenades at spot you want. That pretty much means that you get 10 types of grenades for almost every type, if you can use AI effectively. Awesome. Also, look, finally have supressed sniper rifle.
AI of your teammates were supposedly improved. They cover each other while advancing, one overlooking while another moves in. What I felt however is how often I would bump into their fat collision boxes while backpedalling away from corner, with them refusing to move away without order. And how slow they moved toward cover which I told them to, due to covering each other. Because on practise when you order them to get behind certain cover you usually want them to get there ASAP.
Campaign itself is awesome though. Plot isn't as good, but those missions are much better. Still punishing, it feels more challenging. More good spots to use smoke grenades, sometimes more good entrances. Enemies are much more awesome, looking professional and with bad intentions, having laser sights to show off. And yep, they still show off personality, with all the behind-wall talks.
Oh, and they brought enemies with shield this time around, so you know that you want to flank them while AI does frontal assault. Or abuse sniper rifle, it still works. And it still mixes open fight with room clearing, so you don't get tired of either sniping or breaching.
Too bad that pre-last chapter makes you go solo. It's very hard, yes, but without teammates it's just boring sniping with smoking.
Now, other modes. You can play campaign in coop with one more person if you want, seamlessly. You can't revive each other, nope. AI teammates are still around, only host can command them. It's easier with friend, yes. Especially when it ends only when both are dead in same time, you can just hide and wait for respawn.
Then there is Terrorist Hunt. You can now play it with AI teammates too when in offline mode, but it still feels extremely scripted in how terrorists spawn. It's predictable and frustrating, artificial. However, once you get online, it becomes super fun for some reason. Terrorist spawn feels more natural with 4 players going around and it gets more intense, with difficulty being just right. Fear the terrorist with SPAS-12 shotgun, he is going to be your main demise. It sure gets tense when you are the last person online and there is only one terrorist left, with shotgun. You don't know where he spawned and they are really good at travelling around map.
It does sometimes feel that baiting tactic work much better than actually clearing from all the sides. But oh well. Maybe it could use Hostage Rescue mode.
Oh yea, there is Versus mode too. Maybe it was great in other Versus modes, but people play only DM these days. I tried. It was awful. People sprinting around, stopping only to shoot right into faces. Like other bad realistical shooters. Try to get more tactical in Team Deathmatch by overwatching territory and you are mostly likely will be called out as camper.
But overall, the plot doesn't feel as interesting or urgent in this part and it doesn't have much of new, but it's still an improvement in everything else and is really good Rainbow Six title.

I really, REALLY wanted to love Beatbuddy. Games that incorporate music into their gameplay are kind of my thing, and to the game's credit it does start out VERY strong. The first half hour or so is incredibly fun and inventive as you experience how the game layers beats on top of each other to create the main song of the level, and discovering each new creature and how it interacts with the soundtrack and Beatbuddy gameplay wise is incredibly novel. Sadly the gameplay fails to stay fresh for very long, relying on the same bounce pad and reflector tile gameplay for the majority of the game, which is pretty disappointing for a game that's only 3 hours long.
The first thing you'll notice are how floaty the controls feel. The game (appears) to be set underwater, so that point can be somewhat forgiven, but if you're playing with a keyboard and mouse the poor controls are really put front and center. The majority of the game is based upon interacting with your environment, using keys in locks, hitting things to the beat, etc. However this quickly becomes INFURIATING when Beatbuddy simply refuses to pick up an object or swim a certain direction, ESPECIALLY in time sensitive situations. I can count on one hand the times during my playthrough that Beatbuddy picked up or placed an object where I wanted to the first time without having to click the mouse repeatedly. Another totally bizarre control issue is that Beatbuddy will occasionally just stop listening to your commands altogether and swim in completely random directions, sometimes coinciding with your mouse being over the foreground art but sometimes due to nothing at all. All this leads to a very obnoxious gameplay experience at best, and a potentially maddening one at worst. Eventually you get used to it (about 30 minutes before the end, unfortunately) but when the game throws handfuls of enemies at you at once and you're being helplessly knocked around while the game ignores mouse input, or given a time sensitive puzzle and Beatbuddy flat out REFUSES to pick up an essential piece of the puzzle in a timely manner, you can't help but feel let down.
Thankfully Beatbuddy is forgiven some of its gameplay missteps with a very charming art style, which is a 3D character model on top of very beautiful layered 2D art, although for a musically driven game the soundtrack is surprisingly mediocre, save for a few standouts. While the first level is designed extremely well in regards to introducing not only the layers of song throughout the level in a gradual and fun way, but also the creatures of the world and how they interact with you and the song, that detail seems to go out the window past the first few levels. The soundtrack becomes just the backdrop as the game progresses instead of a major gameplay element, with a few exceptions of course. The fact that the game forgoes a lot of these fun ways to introduce the song of the level compounded with the hit or miss controls and the fact that you see most of what the gameplay has to offer very early on makes the Beatbuddy segments seem like filler until you get to the next vehicle sequence, which is when you get to hear the level's song in its entirety (or as much as they were allowed to play, as the "level's song in its entirety" actually only ever ends up being maybe a 15 second loop of a chunk of the chorus). It began to feel like I was just chugging through the same old bounce pad, reflector tile and collect the gems sequences as Beatbuddy until I got to play the next vehicle segment, which turned out to be the game I ACTUALLY wanted to play.
As for the story, it serves its purpose. For a 3 hour game it does its job. The characters are all very likeable and cute, too. Their designs are pretty unique and fit the world well, and they all speak in their own style of beatbox which is pretty endearing. The game has some decent humor in the way of your companion, Clef, dismissing the very clearly falling apart vehicle you both ride in and the Prince character doing some very tongue-in-cheek villain things. Slight spoiler alert here, but the ending seems to happen all at once and with very little fanfare which is very disappointing. For a big, boisterous music game I was expecting a large boss battle with some rousing music, but the ending really comes out of nowhere and happens very quietly. For a short little music game like this I suppose it's fine, I was just hoping for more.
Even with all that being said, there's still something about Beatbuddy. I'd be totally lying if I said a few of the songs weren't still stuck in my head, and I beat it in one sitting and didn't want to stop, which is saying a lot nowadays. Maybe it was because I wanted to see what the next level was going to look like, or what new mechanic they would introduce, or maybe I just wanted to hear what the next song would be. Unfortunately with the gameplay flaws and short gametime Beatbuddy comes off as less of a good videogame and more of a really enjoyable interactive music video. If that's fine to you, by all means pick up this game. If you're really pining for a new music game, pick up this game. For everyone else I'd say maybe avoid this one. Pick up some of the greats (Audiosurf, Beat Hazard, etc.) or maybe get it on sale.

Don't buy this game at full price. If it's heavilly discounted, think about giving it a go. Maybe.

7 years after its release, it has seen radical changes.
2 years ago, I was misinformed that I must purchase this game to continue playing. After so much searching the Internet I was convinced that I am one of grandfathered in Quake Live on Steam and thus exempt from purchase.
Compared to its older counterparts, like Quake III Arena and OpenArena, it is noticeably more difficult and even worse, take forever to master because of its internals have been changed in a way that the feeling is slightly different, like Rocket Launcher being fired bit closer from the point of view.
I am dissapointed that some who have misused their admin privileges in their servers, and players who have abused the vote system in a way that is unsubstantiated, an act of senseless discrimination, and unfair to new players, for whatever reason.
However, there are Race and Quake III DeFRaG-like servers that are far less affected by players' tyrannical misuse and rigging. Since players can't frag each other and instead limited by their skills of movement and weaponry manoeuvres, there are often many text and audiovisual tutorials on strafe jumping and weapon boosting/jumping prior to debut of Race gametype in Quake Live.
Most techniques in Quake III DeFRaG can also be used in Quake Live.
Some, such as strafe jumping, is slower than in Quake III DeFRaG.
Others, like plasma ground boosting (CPM) and overboucing don't work in Quake Live.
Being a game based on a game engine (Id Tech 3) programmed 18 years ago, Quake Live can run on essentially any modern computer to date and in many situations, up to and over 125 frames per second.

As the name implies, Quake Live is probably the definitive online title of the franchise, further refining and technologically improving on Quake 3’s numerous experiences. Multiplayer in its purest form.

HellDivers is a Hardcore, 4-player co-op, top-down shooter that seems to be a hybrid of Alien Swarm, Magicka, and Diablo. Thematically, you'll be reminded of every Sci-Fi trope that you can imagine as you travel around the galaxy, meet new and interesting species, and act as an ambassador of Democracy. Think.... Starship troopers.
Positives:
+The action and gameplay of shooting up aliens as a spaceman is very well done.
+The progression system system is very well-done. Leveling is as you'd expect- get levels, unlock skins and weapons. Players can also unlock new strategems (powers) by playing through a series of missions successfully. Lastly, players must accrue research points (through leveling and collecting samples on maps) to upgrade their gear. This is a sort of talent tree for your character.
+Equipping your character individually, as well as a team, presents a lot of interesting and meaningful choices. You only have 4 strategem (power) slots, a weapon, and perk (big power) that you can equip. Much of the fun is the trial and error of different loadouts for you and for your team.
+There is a huge variety of weaponry. Most of the weapons are different enough that there's not really a 'super weapon' but rather weapons that fit a specific roll or style.
+There is a massive variety of powers that you can unlock. Think of Guild Wars/Guild Wars 2 - the possibilities are immense.
+The combined arms aspect of the game is well-done.
+BIG ROBOTS that you can use to spread Democracy.
Negatives:
-There are occasionally steam network/game connectivity issues. If you disconnect from a mission,  you lose your progress in collecting science samples (which are really important.)
-You absolutely must stay on the same screen as your teammates. This can get a little hectic/difficult if your cursors are scattered all over the place, constraining your ability to see what's going on around you.
-The controls can be a little hard to master. Your mouse cursor will move faster than your characters/turrets can turn. Ultimately, there's some balance to this... but many PC players will find this to be a bit sluggish.
-When playing with randoms, there is a (small) potential that you will encounter a hacker; reportedly, a hacker can increase your XP/science points to max, somewhat thwarting your progression.
Overall, this is a great game to play with your buddies looking for a Coop game, or with random folks and pubbies. The action is good, and there is a lot of value in the hilarious wipes that you'll surely incur.

I strongly recommend this game if you like action/RPGs. It's one of the best in the Ys series to date, perhaps only bested now by Memories of Celceta. It's a blast to play, has a lot of content, and the game doesn't get bogged down by lengthy dialog scenes.

Ys Origin does a great job explaining the past, it also features interesting characters that you can finish the game with (each one having their own unique game-play, equipment, short storyline and so).
For those who don't know, Ys is an old school action RPG (from the late 80's) that luckily didn't got extinct in today's modern video game industry (That strives to approach to the masses), the surviving series features a very solid and hardcore experience for those who delve in to it (No hands are held here, not suitable for some casual players).
Without delving that much in to the storyline, I'll start by saying that the whole game is set in a massively big tower with tons of floors where you'll actively explore till you reach the top, all because due to the fact you're part of a team that is looking for two mysterious female angel like characters who have disappeared and also they are fighting a mysterious evil that suddenly appeared on their land.
Just like the first of the series, it is based on your character progression (Status), based on your skill and how well prepared and equipped you're, you'll fight tons of different minions and bosses through out the game.
The game is fast paced, if you're used to a slower and less action based game, then do not delve in to this one, you'll have to be quick and prepare yourself to evade any possible attacks and at the same time plan how you'll attack your foes quickly before their defense is up again.
You're forced to play the game to unlock new areas as you progress but do take in mind that you're not only forced to a narrow path, you'll have some freedom of exploration to farm and grab new items.
As for the game soundtrack you'll be delighted, it is so memorable!
In terms of art style and UI they are all professionally done and will set in motion your connection to the game, giving you a taste of immersion (You'll have a good read, the game has a big script), character wise; some are forgettable but overall your experience with them is quite positive.
If you like Anime and you like oldschool games that are fast paced and hard, then this is the game for you!

Slash it 2 is an action puzzle game. Some what of a cross between Guitar Hero / Rock band and typing games.
The game Kind of feels a lot like those typing games I use to play on the old school apple and mac computers as a kid. Where the try to integrate typing into a fun game, and the game delivers on that aspect. The game is very simple and anyone with knowledge of letters and numbers can play it.
I reached level 5 my first time playing with the numbers, (I used the number pad, not sure if its cheating, but it seemed a lot easier that way) I made it to level 8, after my first run with letters. It was interesting and fun. Kind of intense at times.
The music goes along to every letter or number dropped, making the game have a nice rhythm aspect to it. & The music is good, the music is one of the most solid things about the game.
The Colors are very bright, vibrant and nice, they have a psychedelic feel crossed over with the lights and videos you might see when attending a rave, the boxes and circles and everything kind of seem generic though in my opinion.
Now while it does have a high scores list from other players online you can try to rack up points against and try to beat, I still Would like to see a multiplayer mode where the players actually go head to head live, if they make a part 3, it could be easily done I believe.
I Personally enjoy the game, but its not something i'd play all the time by any means. However, the game is fun.
The biggest pro of the game is the massive amounts of achievements that it has, 303, yes, THREE HUNDRED and THREE achievements. That is insanity. That is the best part about buying it, that and it having trading cards, make the game worth the purchase alone, but I think more could be done with the user interface to make it look less generic.
Other than that decent game.
I did not purchase the DLC, but was glad to see that it does have it, and you can get your game pimped out with 6 more songs per DLC pack, they are cheap only a buck a piece, they looked cool, but the chinese one really through me off, how am I suppose to type chinese letters without actually knowing chinese lol.
Good for the songs at least though I guess.

So i may have low hours, but i have already finished the campaign, and have a couple things to say, and recommend for the game. Dying light is absolutly amazing. Great story and gameplay. But not every game is perfect.
Pros:
-Parkour is amazing. Very well done and makes you feel like a badass.
-Endless hours of gameplay. Your definitly getting your moneys worth.
-The story is interesting. Has that kind of effect you would see in The last of us. (going with that because no spoilers)
-Online play is very smooth. Ive never encountered any kind of connection issues or bugs so far.
-Open world.
Cons:
-The game is very slow at the start If you dont have the DLC. For about 1-2 hours maybe you spend half your time wumping zombies with a table leg or a plank or just running from them alltogether.
-Some of the bossfights are insanely hard on your own. Its somewhat annoying because not very many people are playing this game anymore.
-The Bozak Hoard DLC is near impossible to complete on your own
-The Following DLC can be annoying sometimes, because every time you get in your car you will attract maybe 3-4 virals which are very annoying to get away from because they are as fast as your car.
-Lots and lots of bugs. From NPC's falling through the ground to your character acting like hes missing numerous braincells (Jumping the wrong way off a wall, not grabbing a ledge or grabbing the wrong ledge, getting stuck, etc.)
-Be the zombie "goons" Are massive zombies with heavy rebars that can do a ton of damage to you, and knock you down. They spawn on the last 3 nests and i feel this is very unfair for the survivors.
As for the Be The Zombie mode, ive found it very difficult and tedious to win against 1 person when being the zombie. Certain factors are a little bit unfair in the mode. The hunter cant do anything to you while in the radious of a flare except watch helplessly as you destroy a nest, or try to distract them by tackling and slamming which will most likely fail against experienced players. And these are the problems i have with just 1 person. With 4, if they stay grouped up, the hunter pretty much has absolutly no chance of winning. Unlimited UV flashlights, Flares, etc. Can really make the game unbalanced. The hunter also dies way too fast. Surround him with a group and hes pretty much instantly dead. Respawn times for the hunter are a bit too long also. Your gonna be dying alot as a hunter against 4 people. So a faster respawn time wouldnt hurt. Also "goons" Are massive zombies with heavy rebars that can do a ton of damage to you, and knock you down. They spawn on the last 3 nests and i feel this is very unfair for the survivors.
The game also does a very poor job at showing you where to go, this is mainly a problem with main story quests, or even some of The Following DLC side quests. I understand why they didnt put much effort into that part of the game though, because the game isnt based around the main story, as are all open world games. So im not heavily bothered by this.
Overall, the game is very good, but like i said, no game is perfect. Based on the game itself without any dlc, id give it a 7/10. As for the DLC in the game, id say The Following DLC is all you really need. 5.5/10 for the DLC. Would i recommend at full price? No. The game is in too much of a broken state atm. Updates are still coming in, but it seems they only really care for content drops rather then fixing bugs.

Short TL,DR Version:
PROS:
+Lots of achievements
+Cheap
CONS:
-Bad Music & Sounds
-Uninteresting Visuals
-Unbalanced & Broken Gameplay
ACHIEVEMENT COUNT: 438
TRADING CARDS: Yes (7 Cards, 3 Free drops)
Long Review:
I first saw this game back in Jan 2017. As someone who plays idle clicker games, seeing "new take on clicker genre" I thought that i'd give it a go, but the game had a "Q1 2017" release. Cut to today (13th May 2017), when I saw the game had finally become purchaseable. I bought it, installed and clicked play.
And boy, what a absolute letdown...where to start?
MUSIC: one track in the game, and it's a generic "happy" song, which not only doesn't suit the game at all, it's there from the moment you start it up, to the moment you click the mute button.
SOUND FX: Terrible. Imagine a lvl-up sound, or a hitting sound, or a pick-up sound. Your sounds are probably better than what's in this game. Plus, the lvl-up sound is FAR louder than anything else (yes, even music), so prepare to be blindsided by it.
VISUALS: Clashing. The UI "wood" graphics and pale blue background don't change at all throughout the game, making them stagnant around an hour in. The area backgrounds (all 1 square inch of them) are decent and the egg monsters designs are nice (though completely ripped from pokemon), but they clash with the pixel graphics of the monsters. Monsters which have a grand total of 3 choppy animation frames.
Edit: The blue background is meant to be a sky. Right... "sky".
GAMPLAY: Worst part of it.
It's tried to combine an idle clicker with a monster RPG, and it's come off weaker because of it. Monsters aren't caught, they're just randomly added to your group.
Lvling up a monster just paves the way for more DPS, which you don't need because there a handy "+#DPS for $" button which is always there and never increase in price.
Only the first 3 wild monsters can get DPS equipment (robotic upgrades) from gold chests (which rarely show up), but it can't be equipped until iLvl50+ AND spend large sums of money on said equipment.
The egg that you get at the start doesnt really matter, because the ability is the exact same (2xmonster lvl as click strength (+1 because the dev loves odd numbers)).
There's no point to train up any more than 1 wild monster because there is no time limit on the enemy monsters.
Aside from cash, the resources (bronze,silver and gold bars) have no real point, aside from a few minor upgrades.
Other Notes:
This game has a ton of achievements. 400+ i think. But they're all earn X money, kill X monsters, etc. Plus, they're not spaced out. At all. So you WILL earn around 150 in the first 15 minutes.
Unlike other clickers, because this game isn't free, you DO NOT have do micro-transactions to get all the trading cards (small consolation but hey, better than nothing)
Final Verdict:
Unless you want lots of achievements on your profile, stay far away from this game. It's not balanced, not interesting and not worth your time.

This game is amazing and if you like Star Wars I can't think of a reason why you wouldn't like it. If you don't like Star Wars, but you do like FPS games, then all I can say is that in my opinion this is a very good game, and I'm certainly not alone in thinking that. The only downside is the aged graphics, but I find you forget about that really quickly.
If you like playing singleplayer, you can create playlists of a large selection of varied maps, a decent number of game modes, and you can also select whether to play in the era of the prequels or the original trilogy. The gameplay is good and there are several classes to choose from that offer varied gameplay. There is also a mechanic that allows you to play as or against one of the heroes from the movies. They are very powerful but since they are alone and have a long cooldown on spawns, it's more or less balanced.
The era selection thing I mentioned earlier ties into the story of the game. It follows a company of clone/storm troopers from being part of the republican army throughout the rise of the empire, and it's really good. You will learn a few things that you might not have realised, but mainly you get to experience the familiar story through a different perspective. There are a few missions that you'll recognise from the movies, and it's really nice when you see them. In my opinion, at the price it's being sold at (certainly during a sale, anyways), the campaign alone is enough to make it worth your purchase.
As for multiplayer... I sort of don't want to say anything because I'm not sure myself what the situation is currently. The official servers are indeed shut down, but there are apparently still lots of fan servers running. I have played on some of these and didn't have any problems, however when I tried again later on I wasn't able to do it. I think I might have just accidentally blocked the game in my firewall or something, but I don't want to promise anything. Basically I don't know♥♥♥♥♥♥about multiplayer, look somewhere else if that is very important to you.
Honestly if you're reading this, that probably means you're already interested, and I think you should just go for it. It's a great game and it's money well spent.

My anti-tank squad is hunkered down behind a wooden fence. They're pinned down by heavy machine gun fire originating directly in front, preventing them from peppering the medium German tank to their right with RPGs. A few feet ahead of them is a structure where they could find temporary shelter, but making a break for it would be suicide. To make matters worse, they are freezing to death. Too long in the harsh winter away from a warming fire or holed up inside a bunker and they'll start dropping like flies. An AT shell penetrates the vulnerable rear of the Nazi tank; my heavy AT gunners have finally finished turning their confiscated weapon toward the enemy. As the German treads whirl to face the new threat and the heavy machine gunners move to support it, my anti-tank squad takes the opportunity to hop the fence and makes it safely inside the house. RPG fire soon whizzes from the broken windows, striking the Axis armor. The tank is almost destroyed, but my AT gunners are getting cut down, soon too weak in number to man their weapon. Machinery roars like an angry beast as the smoking, crushed tank turns its' wounded turret toward the building and the German machine gunners pivot in the snow. There's a high pitched whine. Then a BOOM. The tank explodes. The Axis gunners try to retreat, but the bullets raining from the occupied building prove too much for them. They soon fall, shot in the back while trying to run. My mortar team emerges from the tree line and a group of engineers are not far behind, ready to build a fire for my dwindling army. That was only one tank down, and there were half a dozen more hiding somewhere in the cold Soviet night.
Company of Heroes 2 works spectacularly on the micro level.  Maneuvering squads to ensure they have adequate cover and numbers to take on the enemy creates some truly impressive sights.  The more-zoomed-in-than-usual view makes for an experience not unlike watching a war movie being filmed from up high.  You're not just sending icons to meet enemy icons and hoping your rock beats their scissors or depending on a random roll of the dice to determine victory.  Moving each soldier into advantageous positions is nothing short of vital.  This is both a strength and weakness of the game.  If you don't babysit your crews expect them to make some questionable decisions.  They'll stand in the middle of the road as a tank rolls right up to them and cuts them to ribbons, or march right through an enemy stronghold without firing a shot.  The AI and pathfinding are questionable, so be prepared for a lot of clicking or a lot of dead soldiers.
I'm not ashamed to admit I'm not well versed in real time strategy games, having only dabbled in a handful over the years. The aesthetic and setting of Company of Heroes definitely had me engaged and willing to learn more than most other genre offerings, but some legacy problems (for me, anyway...) kept me from a long term engagement.  The fourteen campaign missions are entirely staged affairs, and aside from a general overview of what you're meant to accomplish you're going in blind.  You could build up to the (small) population cap with mostly foot soldier fodder, running over enemy forces with impunity, only to run into a wall of tanks later that decimate them with a ticking timer or other encroaching objective looming that ensures you're ♥♥♥♥ed and need to reload a save or start the entire mission over again.  These are beginner's traps, and that's not good design.  You'll find ways to finish the battles eventually as you learn the requirements and the basics of the game, but that's not a good alternative to a sufficient tutorial and clear win conditions. A developer in a tutorial video encourages you to “watch YouTube videos” and “check with the community on forums” to learn the game, which “requires hundreds of hours to fully comprehend”... Maybe a bullet point for some, but personally I find it to be a little too much to ask.
By the end of the campaign (on Easy) I was starting to get the basics down, but was running out of true single player content.  There are some skirmishes to check out and bot matches, but jumping into these scenarios seemed a bit useless at that point: more learning of specific skill sets to an overall game I'm probably not going to get much deeper into.  There's multiplayer, of course, for those who are interested in that.. but I'm not ready to jump into the meat grinder against RTS animals who have been playing Company of Heroes 2 (and only Company of Heroes 2) non-stop since it released two years ago.
I don't know if I'll continue playing the game further or not, but I experienced the game as a solid 18 hour single player diversion.  It was fine for a casual RTS player like myself.  The WWII action is visceral and immediate, and moving platoons around the battlefield is satisfying if occasionally frustrating.  CoH2 doesn't seem to entirely escape from the genre trappings that I find rather off-putting, but taken as a chance to play weekend armchair general on the set of Saving Private Ryan it was enjoyable.

Do not hesitate, buy it now. This is the first time in over a year I truly enjoyed playing a video game.

-If you enjoyed Alien Swarm any at all this is right up your alley.
-If you enjoyed Magicka but you're like me and not into magic-fantasy stuff, this is a sci-fi version of Magicka with guns.
-If you enjoyed watching Starship Troopers (SST) like I did when I was a child then this is definitely for you, and people like you are why we were at the Bug homeworld within a few days and nowhere close to the Illuminate and Cyborg homeworlds. Lol.
Seriously this game hits the SST vibe really hard from the first movie with the humorous propaganda and overall vibe. Add in the bugs and you have a pretty close analogue to a modern SST game if playing the bugs. The meta game is also more fun that I originally though, I'm now choosing the front closest to the home system to fight on so we won't risk having to defend ourselves. Most people are hitting the bugs as of this post during the first war and we got to the homeplanet like 2nd day of release, and the Illumanati systems are about 1 notch further along than the cyborg. I think lots of people think like me and are playing the Cyborgs to simply shore up that weak spot but it's also an advancing front so we are advancing on all 3 fronts. Maybe in the next war cycle the devs will adjust numbers and make it harder to progress.
All the kit in the base game works fine. In fact I just bought the DLC megapack and only used one of the items tonight, I still mostly use the base-game stuff. Everything has it's use, it will suck most of the time if used inproperly. While the DLC are not needed if you enjoy this game they give you more options to further tune your play style to a specific situation but you are not missing anything critical just by being in the base game. Typically DLC are a neg to me but this game does it right, the new stuff isn't OP nor is it useless/cosmetic-only.
On to criticisms. Aiming is made for controllers, so your character always starts aiming in front of them and you have to sweep to your target. You get used to it within a few hours of play, no problem. It's a minor annoyance we cannot have the crosshair always on to see where we are aiming though, this is just a bad oversight of the port from Playstation. The random 'funny' deaths are only funny if you play this game lightly. When playing serious and the game decides to land a pod 10ft away from the beacon right on you instead that's not funny at higher levels. The game is designed with a poor camera system too, the camera hovers in the middle of the entire squad, spread out too much and you can't see enemies at the edges before they run into your guy. This forces a squad to stick together, but this forced closeness also causes lots of accidental deaths from friendly fire to drop pods landing in such close quarters etc. This is by design, this game is made to be difficult and for you to die. Having a low-death count is not necessary, it's just a sign of skill.
Overall besides a few minor negatives I would call Helldivers GOTY material since we are close to Christmas. All year 2015 nothing entertained me like the recent PC release of Helldivers. Entry price is $20 and you will have everything needed in-game to be a top-shelf player if you do your part. The $40 pack with all DLC is worth it, otherwise you have to pay $25 for all the DLC in a megapack after buying the base game or like $45 for all the DLC individually. If $40 makes you balk then just spend the $20 and call it a good enjoy the game, that's like the price of 3 footlongs from subway.

What a game!
Traverse through space with an alien crew and randomly battle spaceships! Every playthrough of FTL is different, but thoroughly enjoyable. If you play this game, you will lose. Sometimes terribly. Sometimes, everything will be going extremely well and seconds before the boss, an insignificant event will lead to the destruction of your ship. Sometimes you'll die on your second jump in sector 1! Often, when this happens, you'll learn for next time. ;)
The first time I beat this game was after 50 unsuccessful hours and about 50 different runs. At the time, there were only two game modes: easy, and normal. I always chose easy. I would occasionally feel frustrated ("this game is so hard!") before I finally won, but the feeling of victory after all those games... Mmm... Worth it!
I played FTL quite a bit before unlocking a few ships. Setting a goal of unlocking ships helps make the runs enjoyable, especially if you're struggling. Unlocking these ships allows you to experiment with different ship structures. Your gameplay style might be compatible with a ship that isn't unlocked by default. For example, I'm a big fan of boarding ships, but no "base" ships come with a teleporting pad that can hold 4 members. Only after unlocking the Mantis ship was I able to enjoy a ship with awesome boarding capabilities. I also don't like to use missiles because they're non-renewable. The components of your ship can and will be very different every run, and you might not know ahead of time what kind of ship you'll be playing. Will you find drone parts right away? Will you get a boost that makes it useful to do cloaking? The random events make it hard to anticipate the future. That's part of the fun. :)
Some of the game mechanics aren't immediately obvious, which set me back a little bit. For example, it took me a while to realize that if you look at your enemy's ship, you can deduce what kind of weapon they'll fire -- something very important for determining whether to stay or fight. Once, I (accidentally) sent my crew members to a swift death on a scout vessel that had no oxygen. There are a lot of subtleties to the game that are sometimes learnt the hard way. Once again, it's part of the fun.
I also want to take the time to highlight the soundtrack of this game. It's really, really good. This is coming from someone who rarely notices music in games.
I really like everything about this game: the randomness, the fun events, the ability to micromanage your crew, the ability to suffocate the enemy ship by depriving them of oxygen, etc. There are per-ship achievements and global achievements that are fun; there are special quests to unlock ships that give the game replay value.
This is definitely one of my favorite games, I heartily recommend it!

Good:

Bad:
* All of the polish around The Flame is pretty lackluster. Not having an intro or closing cutscene really leaves me hanging for some personality. Like, he seems to have some in the facial animations and between-phase cutscenes, but it feels pretty sparse compared to the main cast and for a dude built on revengance, I really wanted more out of the non-fight stuff. I also know I'm gonna go back and put more time into it, because this game makes me want to play better for my own satisfaction. It's great. Buy it.

If you've enjoyed "The Room", then you'll like this.  If you haven't, then go look at that first.  (You don't
to have played the first game, but it definitely helps.)
The first game was themed around a single nested puzzle-box, solving the one inside once it has been extracted from the outer layer.  This game takes a different approach, with several unrelated rooms each containing multiple separate but related puzzles.  (Solving all the puzzles in one room takes you to the next, which has a different theme.)
There's a greater focus on magic in this game as well, with more use of the eyepiece and more elements requiring lining up symbols.  To be honest, I felt these were the weakest parts of the game and I would have preferred more physical puzzles like the first game, but there was still enough of that to keep things interesting.
The story established in the first game continues to this one (and also somewhat explains why the puzzles are laid out like that), and you're treated to a cutscene at the end that ties things together nicely.  Though there's obviously still something to discover, as there's another game in this series still to come.
Ultimately I don't think I personally enjoyed this one quite as much as the prior game (though it's hard to say for sure), but it was still a lot of fun and the environments are still gorgeous, and I still recommend it to anyone that enjoyed the prior game.  The varied environments and themes can help to keep interest up, especially so if you particularly liked the magical themes towards the end.

Do not get me wrong, 4 was good in its own aspect, but 3 was a better game in my opinion. The story was better, hit detection seemed better, and the gang and law enforcement interaction in 3 was better. Being able to get "stars" with each faction was interesting and made the game quite intense. I also laughed so much more in 3 than I did in 4. In 4, the game was nuts from the beginning. Loved the weapons, loved the powers, just only wished you could actually fly. Also, the end of the game really left much more to be desired. The beginning was AMAZING, but it kind of trickled off.

Truly, what made me the most excited about this game was the fact that I could import my character from Saints Row 3. It was awesome to carry on that character's story from the hundreds of hours I played on Saints Row 3 to the new Saints Row 4. I honestly felt that the idea was a bit "Matrix-ie" and was basically like bringing Neo into a game that actually was fun. Coincidently, my character was dressed like he was from the Matrix in Saints Row 3, which brought me a chuckle.
I enjoy the "over the top" aspect that this game brings and how this game does not start off slow. Though the ending was not great, nor does it really make sense to me. I mean, when you are flying around Steelport, why have cars in the first place? Granted as you advance in the game, cars become weapons, so there is that.
I would play this game again, but only with a friend after beating the game on solo mode. I would recommend it to someone who likes crazy, over the top games as well. I enjoyed it, but on a scale of 1-10, my replay factor is about a 4. Put Saints Row 3 on though, I’m down for HOURS!

Ys Origin does a great job explaining the past, it also features interesting characters that you can finish the game with (each one having their own unique game-play, equipment, short storyline and so).
For those who don't know, Ys is an old school action RPG (from the late 80's) that luckily didn't got extinct in today's modern video game industry (That strives to approach to the masses), the surviving series features a very solid and hardcore experience for those who delve in to it (No hands are held here, not suitable for some casual players).
Without delving that much in to the storyline, I'll start by saying that the whole game is set in a massively big tower with tons of floors where you'll actively explore till you reach the top, all because due to the fact you're part of a team that is looking for two mysterious female angel like characters who have disappeared and also they are fighting a mysterious evil that suddenly appeared on their land.
Just like the first of the series, it is based on your character progression (Status), based on your skill and how well prepared and equipped you're, you'll fight tons of different minions and bosses through out the game.
The game is fast paced, if you're used to a slower and less action based game, then do not delve in to this one, you'll have to be quick and prepare yourself to evade any possible attacks and at the same time plan how you'll attack your foes quickly before their defense is up again.
You're forced to play the game to unlock new areas as you progress but do take in mind that you're not only forced to a narrow path, you'll have some freedom of exploration to farm and grab new items.
As for the game soundtrack you'll be delighted, it is so memorable!
In terms of art style and UI they are all professionally done and will set in motion your connection to the game, giving you a taste of immersion (You'll have a good read, the game has a big script), character wise; some are forgettable but overall your experience with them is quite positive.
If you like Anime and you like oldschool games that are fast paced and hard, then this is the game for you!

This game is incredibly atmospheric and completely gorgeous, but that's not what makes it fun to play.  It has an interesting story, immersed with equally interesting side-stories, can be played in any order, and is surprising enough at the end that I didn't really "see it coming" in terms of resolution.  Here's a very short rundown on what it offers and what it doesn't, to help you make a decision on trying it or not.  Note that I'm not making these "pros and cons" as opinion could vary wildly on whether these are good or bad points.  Here's what it offers instead.
What it has:
-a compelling mystery storyline that can be completed in any order (however all parts do need to be completed to see the end)
-a "walking simulator" format that is based almost entirely on exploration with isolated puzzles.  Puzzles vary in complexity (there are walkthroughs available online for the more obscure solutions, but probably aren't necessary for most people experienced with puzzles).
-Stunning graphics.  Bear in mind, however, that if you're running an older computer (like me), you might have to turn down some of the visual settings.  Personally, I spent a few minutes wowing at the scenery and then had to roll back the settings; however, even with lower settings it's a beautiful game.
-A quietly chilling atmophere that is generally not "scary" but maintains a slow, creeping eerieness.  With the exception of one puzzle area that incorporates some jump scares, they keep the horror aspect to the quiet, psychological variety.
What it doesn't have:
-Save points.  The game autosaves at the end of each puzzle area (regardless of the order you complete in), which makes for smooth gameplay but also means that you can't stop mid-puzzle and come back later.  Generally though, the areas are not grossly spread out so restarting from the completion of the previous puzzle doesn't set you back much unless you had mostly finished an area before quitting.
-Combat.  You walk and solve puzzles, but you don't fight anything.  There is a section where you have to avoid a nasty thing, but it'll just set you back to the beginning of the area.
-Tutorial, guidance, or rules.  They tell you flat out at the beginning that they won't hold your hand, and they mean it.  Thankfully, the interface is very simple so at least in that respect, handholding is not necessary.
So that's the nutshell summary of what the game offers.  If you like the walking-simulator style, mysteries, and puzzles, you may like this one.  If you like big action, combat, and explosions, you may not.  Your mileage may vary!

What can I say about Ethan Carter without spoiling it's story? Not a lot other than: I really, REALLY liked it. It's easily one of the most athmospheric and beautiful games I've ever played. The setting, the tone, the influences, the story, the puzzles, everything just worked for me. As I said, I don't want to spoil anything about it, as I think this is one of the games you should come in as freash as you can be, with as little knowledge of it as possible.
It's not a long game, but it also don't have any filler material, only quality stuff. And it's a top experience from start to finish because of that. I think this is also one of the games, that could've been easily messed up, if this would've been some AAA-retail game with 20 hours of content. I really think the lenght is perfect as it is.
If I would have to suggest something, that IMO would've maybe made the game even better, it's probably: few more puzzles would have fitted in, eventhough there are some secrets also.
Only real critique I had with the game is it's saving system: if you have some mystery in the middle of solving and you go and do something and see the "Saving scene...", which usually leads you to believe, that everything you've done/found so far is saved, it doesn't save the mystery that is in the middle of solving. So, just a tip: solve all the mysteries you start before quitting, so you'll avoid playing things thru all over again.
All in all this game is a hell of a debut from the small team hailing from Poland - The Astronauts. And if they'll do more of these narrative game experiences in the future, it'll be a day 1 buy for me. I'm really looking forward what they'll decide to do next.

Review:
“I could feel two kinds of darkness here in Red Creek Valley.The first you walked into, and, with any luck, walked out of. But the other darkness was deeper, stickier, unknowable. And it wanted me to leave.”
The sun is setting over the gorgeous landscape. I enter the empty house that seems desolate and abandoned and pick up a piece of paper. A short story is written on it, the kind of story that tells you a lot about the author. It is written by Ethan Carter, the one I came here to find.
The Vanishing of Ethan Carter is a game thats all about mood and atmosphere. In first person you explore a beautiful and serene environment that contains clues and puzzles, remnants of past events. The more you progress and the closer you look, the more you find out about what happened.
The low-key storytelling and overall gameplay is similar to Gone Home or Ether One. It has a bit more challenging puzzles and more intense moments than Gone Home and is also a bit longer, though still not very long or particularly challenging. I took my time taking everything in and i still was able to finish the game within about 3 hours. The writing, graphics and sound are excellent though and it offers an experience that regards story and atmosphere over challenge or longevity.

Aged a lot better than RS Vegas 1 and is vastly superior in terms of mechanics, enjoyment and replay ability. This is a good example of a sequel doing things right. Sadly it loses some of the mechanics that make the RS Raven Shield/Gold Edition so good such as the tactical compulsive borderline obsessive mission/team planning (which is missed) but to its credit it’s also a lot more streamlined and actually playable (decent controls and graphics which still hold up relatively well).
In Short Rainbow Six is about Squad Based Tactics.  In long...
The single player provides an action packed campaign in which you and your squad can either use stealth to clear rooms of terrorists and take advantage of the element of surprise or go in guns blazing and learn the hard way that your fragile life is easily taken by AI who can even kill you (even in cover) to the point that you end up always sending your squad in first because you realize that the CPU AI is so much better than this at you after you have been spoilt by easy shooters and recovery mechanics. You will hopefully adapt to this and find it much more enjoyable after some brief upset...
There is multiplayer but I'm not really into that. The good news is the progression system for multiplayer spans the whole game so even in single player you gain xp for kills and special points for killing enemy with headshots etc. which unlocks new weapons, outfits, armors, accessories and camouflage patterns. This is something you don’t really see a lot on the single player side of things and adds replay value. The progression system does take a long time to get to the top tier though which was intended for multiplayer longevity i assume.
Other than a campaign (which is also co-op) there is Terrorist Hunt Mode (also co-op) which is a waking nightmare on hard... especially without the AI assisting you. One would assume you are hunting down the terrorists as it is sold to you as a mode of killing all terrorists in the area. The sad truth is it is the terrorists that are in fact hunting YOU (and your friend/team).
In Summary I recommend it on the campaign/mechanics alone. It's a simple and enjoyable game from yesteryear and is a great laugh alone or with a friend.

Now, what to type. This reamake of the incredible game Metro 2033 is definently worth it's price. This game has great atmosphere, visuals, gameplay, story, and other things. After several playthroughs of the original two games and then this, despite some flaws still existing, I can definently say they are two of the best games I have ever played. These two games show how incredible novel based games can be.
Now, the game mechanics. Despite the game being held in the future, it is all but futuristic. With ammo in scarce supply and death lurking in every corner, it definently provides an atmospheric journey through the post-apocalyptic metro tunnels and surface of the remains of Moscow. The gask mask is crucial to survival in this irradiated wasteland. It carries a uniqe mechanic that will determine wether or not you'll survive. The mask not only need filters in order for you to brethe in irradiated areas, but you also need to avoid damage as the mask's visor will break once enough is sustained. Now, this was never a problem for me as I was never in irradiated areas for long enough to suffocate or sustained enough damage to render the mask useless.
Doing that isn't that hard since stealth is also a large mechanic in both games. The ability to stealth largely depends on how you play. Do you approach a room guns ablazing? Or crouched and remain the shadows till the next one? The stealth approach is definently a much better idea then killing everything in sight, as you may be mowed down or mauled if not prepared. Many things can affect how stealthy you are. If you were to fire an unsilenced weapon the enemy will know of your presence; but however, since the weapon silencers are metro-built, they won't completely silence your shot. One way to get around this is to knock out or kill the enemy by getting close enough and knocking out or killing the enemy with a good old right hook or your trench knife. Another method is to use throwing knives, but they are only effective at close-mid range, but they are much more reliable. The best method of silent killing is to use a pneumatic firearm, preferably the Tikhar. The pneumatic firearms are completely silent and are some of the most damaging weapons in the game. The Tikhar is the most versatile pneumatic weapon, as it's a automatic sniper rifle that has abundant and cheap ammo (15mm steel ball bearings). The Helsing is a pneumatic metal bolt (as in crossbow bolt) launcher that has the most expensive but the only reuseable ammo. The two weapons have to be presurized in order to fire and deal damage, the weapons can be over-presurized, but that'll cause the air tanks to leak, trading stealth for the ability to kill enemies in a shot or two; and with the ability to purchase an air tight valve, they will no longer leak and maintain it's tank pressure indefinently. Another thing that needs to be managed is ammo.
The Metro series gives you the ability have the most atmospheric experience possible without the occulus rift: Ranger mode. Ranger mode turns off the hud, crosshairs, and ui as well as making ammo and filters even more scarce than in hardcore, but your weapons and enemies will become more deadly. It is clearly not meant to be the difficulty one would first play the game at, and there is also a ranger hardcore difficulty, which can provide a challenge for survival/FPS video game players. Also what ranger mode will give you is more MGRs.
What MGR stands for is Military-Grade-Rounds. These are used as currency in the metro which can be used at ammo vendors and weapon vendors. The military grade rounds are miles more damaging than the standard 'dirty' rounds produced in the metro. I have never been in a situation where I would need to be firing MGRs to survive but they can be 'hoarded'. At the end of my most recent playthrough of this game I had managed to amass over 1000 MGRs while playing in normal mode, this shows how sparing you can be with your usage of MGRs, but that was also after four playthroughs of the original game so don't be afraid to use them if you need to.
This game is definently an experience, but the animation is somewhat lacking. Not that it would enough to not recomend the game but it can either break the immersion or get a laugh, but it doesn't remove one of the largest thing in the game; how you can't survive the apocolypse any other way. Throughout the game you will meet charcters that will aid you in certain situations by accompanying you, one of the earliest examples is when you are traveling from one station to the next via a railcar. This may sound a bit boring, but, both games have action elements to them to make them more intresting among the hardcore survival of this series. Now this may not be for everyone, as some people don't like on rails segments or situation where you must follow someone.
Exploration is also very cruical to survival. Many resources one can find to maintain survival can be found through exploration, even when you're required to follow someone. The ability to explore is never unused. If there is somewhere you can go, but it isn't required, it's always helpful. Filters, ammo, and weapons can be found through exploration.
So obviously what I'm trying to say is this is an incredible game series. These games show what people are capable of making. With mechanics and gameplay giving a uniqe experience, and despite some (or numerous) flaws, this game is definently worthy of a slot in most's gaming collection along with the game's sequal: Metro Last Light. (Also this review would be longer, but I'd probaly need to playthrough the game, again, again).

My anti-tank squad is hunkered down behind a wooden fence. They're pinned down by heavy machine gun fire originating directly in front, preventing them from peppering the medium German tank to their right with RPGs. A few feet ahead of them is a structure where they could find temporary shelter, but making a break for it would be suicide. To make matters worse, they are freezing to death. Too long in the harsh winter away from a warming fire or holed up inside a bunker and they'll start dropping like flies. An AT shell penetrates the vulnerable rear of the Nazi tank; my heavy AT gunners have finally finished turning their confiscated weapon toward the enemy. As the German treads whirl to face the new threat and the heavy machine gunners move to support it, my anti-tank squad takes the opportunity to hop the fence and makes it safely inside the house. RPG fire soon whizzes from the broken windows, striking the Axis armor. The tank is almost destroyed, but my AT gunners are getting cut down, soon too weak in number to man their weapon. Machinery roars like an angry beast as the smoking, crushed tank turns its' wounded turret toward the building and the German machine gunners pivot in the snow. There's a high pitched whine. Then a BOOM. The tank explodes. The Axis gunners try to retreat, but the bullets raining from the occupied building prove too much for them. They soon fall, shot in the back while trying to run. My mortar team emerges from the tree line and a group of engineers are not far behind, ready to build a fire for my dwindling army. That was only one tank down, and there were half a dozen more hiding somewhere in the cold Soviet night.
Company of Heroes 2 works spectacularly on the micro level.  Maneuvering squads to ensure they have adequate cover and numbers to take on the enemy creates some truly impressive sights.  The more-zoomed-in-than-usual view makes for an experience not unlike watching a war movie being filmed from up high.  You're not just sending icons to meet enemy icons and hoping your rock beats their scissors or depending on a random roll of the dice to determine victory.  Moving each soldier into advantageous positions is nothing short of vital.  This is both a strength and weakness of the game.  If you don't babysit your crews expect them to make some questionable decisions.  They'll stand in the middle of the road as a tank rolls right up to them and cuts them to ribbons, or march right through an enemy stronghold without firing a shot.  The AI and pathfinding are questionable, so be prepared for a lot of clicking or a lot of dead soldiers.
I'm not ashamed to admit I'm not well versed in real time strategy games, having only dabbled in a handful over the years. The aesthetic and setting of Company of Heroes definitely had me engaged and willing to learn more than most other genre offerings, but some legacy problems (for me, anyway...) kept me from a long term engagement.  The fourteen campaign missions are entirely staged affairs, and aside from a general overview of what you're meant to accomplish you're going in blind.  You could build up to the (small) population cap with mostly foot soldier fodder, running over enemy forces with impunity, only to run into a wall of tanks later that decimate them with a ticking timer or other encroaching objective looming that ensures you're ♥♥♥♥ed and need to reload a save or start the entire mission over again.  These are beginner's traps, and that's not good design.  You'll find ways to finish the battles eventually as you learn the requirements and the basics of the game, but that's not a good alternative to a sufficient tutorial and clear win conditions. A developer in a tutorial video encourages you to “watch YouTube videos” and “check with the community on forums” to learn the game, which “requires hundreds of hours to fully comprehend”... Maybe a bullet point for some, but personally I find it to be a little too much to ask.
By the end of the campaign (on Easy) I was starting to get the basics down, but was running out of true single player content.  There are some skirmishes to check out and bot matches, but jumping into these scenarios seemed a bit useless at that point: more learning of specific skill sets to an overall game I'm probably not going to get much deeper into.  There's multiplayer, of course, for those who are interested in that.. but I'm not ready to jump into the meat grinder against RTS animals who have been playing Company of Heroes 2 (and only Company of Heroes 2) non-stop since it released two years ago.
I don't know if I'll continue playing the game further or not, but I experienced the game as a solid 18 hour single player diversion.  It was fine for a casual RTS player like myself.  The WWII action is visceral and immediate, and moving platoons around the battlefield is satisfying if occasionally frustrating.  CoH2 doesn't seem to entirely escape from the genre trappings that I find rather off-putting, but taken as a chance to play weekend armchair general on the set of Saving Private Ryan it was enjoyable.

Do you like DLC?  Do you like burning money on useless skins and other garbage?  Then buy this game.

A fantastic first person platformer with amazing gameplay, beautiful environments, lovable characters and a heartwarming story.  You play a young boy thrown into an unknown world in search of his uncle who has gone missing.
The main feature of this game is, of course, all of the jumping puzzles.  You use a unique suit to launch and grapple your way through the beautiful caves and islands.  Even though you will fall countless times, all of the puzzles are very fun to navigate, and they often include many surrounding areas that can be explored.  This element of exploration is one of the greatest features of the game.  Even when there are not extra areas to explore, there are always fascinating environments to observe, which, at times, easily resemble Terry Gilliam or Studio Ghibli films.
There is no violence, no language and it is not often aggravatingly difficult.  The story is fantastically well written as well, and even though it is not terribly complicated, it is very relatable and interesting.  There are few characters in the game, but the ones that are present are very easy to get attached to.  The game would certainly still be functional with no characters at all, but if that were the case, this game would not be half as good as it is.
truly has something for everyone.  An overall job well done.
